::: {.callout-important}
## Interpretive limits — binding on this document

MOES is a **heuristic prioritisation, not a predictive or clinically validated
model** (project contract, section 7). No statement in this report should be read
as identifying a treatment target or a causal mechanism. Where a conclusion is
provisional it is labelled provisional. Treatment-outcome, survival and
immune-exclusion analyses are out of scope by design.
:::

# Summary

This analysis converts paralog-resolved MYC-family binding in SCLC into
enhancer-anchored regulons and asks whether those regulons retain paralog
identity outside the cell lines they were built from.

**The regulons are internally coherent in cell-line chromatin.** Three of four
pre-registered gate criteria pass ([section 4](#sec-m5)). Leave-one-line-out AUC reaches the
0.70 threshold in `r sum(valid$type == "loo" & valid$auc >= 0.70)` of
`r sum(valid$type == "loo")` held-out lines, and the MYC regulon independently
reproduces the MYC-enhancer→neurogenesis association reported by Plotnik et al.
(OR `r onto$neuro_or[onto$paralog == "MYC" & onto$regulon == "both"]`,
p = `r sprintf("%.0e", onto$neuro_p[onto$paralog == "MYC" & onto$regulon == "both"])`).

**They do not retain paralog identity in patient tumours.** Across
`r sum(rep6$cohort == "GSE60052") * 0 + 160` tumours in two independent cohorts,
neuroendocrine lineage state explains
`r sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(rep6$unique_lineage), max(rep6$unique_lineage))`
of the unique variance in regulon score against
`r sprintf("%.3f–%.3f", min(rep6$unique_paralog), max(rep6$unique_paralog))`
for the paralog's own expression, and no association survives lineage adjustment
in the replication cohort ([section 5](#sec-m6)). This outcome was **pre-registered as a
reportable finding** rather than a failure, and it is reported as one.

**The confound is not an artefact of bulk scoring.** It is present in the
chromatin the regulons were built from, in cell lines, gene-by-gene
genome-wide, and in spatial tissue ([sections 6](#sec-confound) and [9](#sec-m9)).

**Evidence integration returns no prioritised hubs.** Three of four planned
evidence domains were excluded on their own evidence. The two that remain
converge weakly at the top of their rankings — up to
`r sprintf("%.1fx", max(moesglob$max_ratio))` more overlap than chance, global
p `r sprintf("%.3f", min(moesglob$global_p))`–`r sprintf("%.3f", max(moesglob$global_p))`
— but no individual gene survives testing across
`r format(dg("moes_universe_genes"), big.mark = ",")` genes ([section 8](#sec-m8)).

The contribution is therefore the framework, the audit trail, and two
well-characterised negative results — not a hub list.

# Question and gap {#sec-gap}

> How do MYC-associated transcriptional and epigenetic regulatory programmes
> shape SCLC state, and which downstream regulatory hubs are robust enough,
> across independent evidence layers, to warrant further investigation?

Plotnik et al. 2024 established that MYC, MYCN and MYCL1 occupy **distinct
enhancer repertoires** in SCLC cell lines. That is prior work and is not
re-claimed here. Three things were unaddressed and are attempted here:

1. converting paralog-resolved binding into **enhancer-anchored,
   super-enhancer-aware regulons** rather than a promoter/distal split;
2. testing those regulons in **independent human tumour cohorts**, the prior work
   being entirely *in vitro*;
3. prioritising hubs with a **transparent, weight-free integration framework**.

Item 1 succeeded, item 2 produced a negative result, and item 3 produced a null.

# Data

All data are public. No data files are held in version control; they are
reproduced by download scripts against a checksum manifest.

```{r data-table}
d <- data.frame(
  Layer = c("Cell-line chromatin", "Patient tumours", "Cell lines",
            "Functional screen", "Spatial tissue"),
  Source = c("GSE230649 keystone + 9 supporting GEO series",
             "GSE60052 (n=79), George 2015 (n=81)",
             "CCLE / cBioPortal (n=59 SCLC)",
             "DepMap Public 26Q1 (25 SCLC vs 1,183 other lines)",
             "GSE261348 (175 ROI), GSE261345 (121 ROI)"),
  Role = c("MYC-family ChIP, H3K27ac, ATAC — 10 SCLC lines",
           "regulon scoring and replication",
           "lineage association, network feasibility",
           "selective dependency",
           "coherence and orthogonal validation"))
kable(d)
```

Project genome build is **hg19**, mandated by the keystone series. Every
coordinate-handling step asserts the build; hg38 deposits were lifted with loss
rates recorded per file.

```{r fig-s01}
#| fig-cap: "Data landscape: assay coverage per cell line, the genome-build split across deposits, and the limited overlap between MYC-family ChIP lines and lineage-TF control lines."
fig("fig_s01_data_landscape")
```

Assay coverage is uneven by design of the public record rather than by choice.
MYC has five contributing ChIP lines; MYCN and MYCL1 have two each. One line
carries H3K27ac and ATAC but no MYC-family ChIP, and one carries MYC ChIP but no
ATAC. The lineage-TF controls needed for the confounding analysis overlap the
keystone lines only partially — POU2F3 in three, ASCL1 in one, NEUROD1 in none —
which is why resolution of the confound is reported per transcription factor and
never pooled.

# The paralog-resolved regulatory layer {#sec-m5}

```{r fig-m5}
#| fig-cap: "The M5 gate on cell-line chromatin, including the criterion that failed."
fig("fig02_m5_gate")
```

Signal was quantified over an ATAC-defined consensus region universe (no *de
novo* peak calling; the keystone series ships bedGraph only), filtered against
the ENCODE hg19 blacklist v2, stitched into super-enhancers with a knee-point
cutoff, and linked to genes by distance-weighted, activity-correlated linking.
Regulons are the top-ranked genes by aggregate link score.

```{r fig-s02}
#| fig-cap: "Construction of the regulatory layer and the check on each step: threshold calibration, convention stability, the super-enhancer guard, and peak-to-gene linking."
fig("fig_s02_regulatory_pipeline")
```

Two of those steps carry guards added after an initial rule failed. The first
super-enhancer stitching rule returned every stitched enhancer as a
super-enhancer for one line, and was replaced by a knee-point cutoff with a hard
ceiling. Peak-to-gene linking initially assigned distal regions only, which left
promoter-bound genes out of every regulon and understated the enrichment. Both
corrections are recorded in the decision log.

The ATAC threshold is **not load-bearing**: TSS enrichment and H3K27ac fold both
rise monotonically across the whole range tested, so conclusions do not depend on
where the cutoff was placed. The replicate convention, by contrast, does matter,
and is shown rather than hidden — the nesting fraction behind gate criterion 1
varies by only 0.037 within the pre-specified ≥2-replicate rule but sits at
materially different values under the union and all-replicate conventions.

## Gate outcome

```{r gate-table}
g <- gate[, c("criterion", "value", "pass")]
names(g) <- c("Criterion", "Observed", "Pass")
g$Pass <- ifelse(g$Pass, "PASS", "**FAIL**")
kable(g)
```

Criterion 3 — the distal-fraction contrast between MYC-amplified and
MYC-expressing lines — **fails on magnitude while reproducing in direction**
(+3.3 points against a published +27). Contributing factors, none separable at
two lines versus two: the shared ATAC-defined universe is ~84% distal by
construction, which compresses the achievable range; the source study called
peaks *de novo* per line with no shared grid; and one line is absent from DepMap,
leaving the expressing arm at n=2. No significance test is applied, because none
would be honest at that n.

## Internal coherence

Leave-one-line-out AUC reaches the 0.70 threshold in
`r sum(valid$type == "loo" & valid$auc >= 0.70)` of
`r sum(valid$type == "loo")` held-out lines; the exception is MYC/H1048 at
`r valid$auc[valid$type == "loo" & valid$held_out == "H1048"]`. Cross-paralog
Jaccard stays well below the 0.60 limit. This is internal coherence only — it
shows the regulons are not driven by a single contributing line, not that they
transfer to tumours.

## A discordance with the source study

```{r onto-table}
o <- onto[onto$regulon == "both", c("paralog", "hallmark_or", "neuro_or", "neuro_p")]
names(o) <- c("Paralog", "Hallmark OR", "Neurogenesis OR", "Neurogenesis p")
kable(o, digits = 4)
```

The MYC regulon is neurogenesis-weighted, independently reproducing the
enhancer-to-neurogenesis link reported by Plotnik et al. The **MYCN regulon is
not**; it is Hallmark/housekeeping-weighted instead. The source study grouped
MYCN with MYC. This is a discordance, recorded as such.

# Patient-tumour translation {#sec-m6}

```{r fig-m6}
#| fig-cap: "Regulatory programmes lose paralog identity to lineage state in SCLC tumours."
fig("fig01_lineage_dominance")
```

Regulons were scored as mean per-gene z-scores — universe-independent, so the
score does not depend on which other genes were measured — in GSE60052 (n=79) and
replicated in George 2015 (n=81).

## Lineage explains the scores; the paralog does not

```{r m6-table}
r <- rep6[, c("cohort", "paralog", "rho_raw", "rho_partial", "unique_paralog", "unique_lineage")]
names(r) <- c("Cohort", "Paralog", "rho raw", "rho adjusted", "unique R2 paralog", "unique R2 lineage")
kable(r, digits = 4)
```

Unique variance attributable to lineage state exceeds that attributable to the
paralog's own expression by roughly an order of magnitude, in
`r nrow(rep6)` regulon–cohort combinations out of `r nrow(rep6)`. Raw
associations collapse toward zero after adjustment for NE score and all four
lineage transcription factors. In the replication cohort **none survives**; the
single survivor in the discovery cohort is method-dependent and comes from the
regulon that failed programme validation.

If programmes retained paralog identity, the diagonal of the
specificity matrix would dominate. It does not
(`r sum(diag(spec) == apply(spec, 1, max))` of `r nrow(spec)` nominal).

## Power

At n = 79, |rho| ≥ 0.31 was detectable at 80% power. The observed adjusted
associations are well inside that bound, so this is a negative result with power
to support it rather than an absence of evidence.

## Risk R-01 materialised

The project contract pre-registered this outcome: *if paralog-specific regulons
prove inseparable from lineage-TF programmes, the honest conclusion becomes that
MYC-paralog regulatory programmes in SCLC are largely inseparable from lineage
identity, reported as a negative result with a power analysis.* That is what
happened, and that is what is reported.

# The confound at every level tested {#sec-confound}

```{r fig-confound}
#| fig-cap: "The lineage confound is present at chromatin, cell-line and gene level."
fig("fig_s03_lineage_confound")
```

The obvious objection to [section 5](#sec-m6) is that the null is an artefact of tumour-level
scoring. It is not.

```{r confound-table}
c1 <- occ[, c("line", "paralog", "pct_universe_pou2f3", "pct_active_pou2f3", "enrichment")]
names(c1) <- c("Line", "Paralog", "% universe POU2F3-bound", "% active POU2F3-bound", "Enrichment")
kable(c1, digits = 2)
```

**Chromatin.** In the three keystone lines with POU2F3 ChIP, regions active for a
MYC-family paralog are POU2F3-bound at
`r sprintf("%.1f–%.1fx", min(occ$enrichment), max(occ$enrichment))` the rate of
the universe they were drawn from. The entanglement is present before any tumour
is scored. Resolution is uneven across lineage factors and was never pooled:
POU2F3 has three keystone lines, ASCL1 one, NEUROD1 none.

**Cell lines.** MYC expression tracks NE score
(rho `r cellrho$rho[cellrho$paralog == "MYC" & cellrho$target == "NE_score"]`,
FDR `r cellrho$fdr[cellrho$paralog == "MYC" & cellrho$target == "NE_score"]`)
across `r netfeas$n_sclc_lines` CCLE SCLC lines, independently reproducing
Ireland et al. 2020 in a third dataset.

**Genes.** Of 33,682 genes tested per paralog, the number still associated after
lineage adjustment is `r glsum$n_fdr05[glsum$paralog == "MYC"]` (MYC),
`r glsum$n_fdr05[glsum$paralog == "MYCL1"]` (MYCL1) and
`r glsum$n_fdr05[glsum$paralog == "MYCN"]` (MYCN). Survivors are **not**
concentrated in the regulons — enrichment inside versus outside is
OR `r glsum$enrich_or[glsum$paralog == "MYC"]`
(p `r glsum$enrich_p[glsum$paralog == "MYC"]`) for MYC — so they do not rescue
the paralog-specific claim.

# Functional evidence {#sec-m7}

```{r fig-m7}
#| fig-cap: "Functional evidence supports the regulon genes collectively, not any one paralog."
fig("fig03_functional_domain")
```

## Regulon genes carry selective dependency, collectively

```{r dep-table}
e <- enr[, c("paralog", "regulon_tested", "n_selective", "or", "ci_low", "ci_high", "p")]
names(e) <- c("Paralog", "Genes tested", "Selective", "OR", "CI low", "CI high", "p")
kable(e, digits = 3)
```

Pooled across all three regulons the enrichment is real:
OR `r pooled$or` (95% CI `r pooled$ci_low`–`r pooled$ci_high`),
p = `r signif(pooled$p, 3)`, on `r pooled$selective_in` selective genes in
`r format(pooled$n_regulon_genes, big.mark = ",")` tested. Because dependency is
not expression, this domain escapes the lineage confound that removed the
transcriptional domain.

**It is not paralog-resolved.** The per-paralog odds ratios differ by one gene
and their confidence intervals overlap almost completely. MYCL1's nominal
p = `r enr$p[enr$paralog == "MYCL1"]` carries a 95% CI of
`r enr$ci_low[enr$paralog == "MYCL1"]`–`r enr$ci_high[enr$paralog == "MYCL1"]`,
which **includes 1**: Fisher's exact p and its conditional interval disagree at
these counts, which is itself a reason not to read a per-paralog verdict. The
pooled test is the powered question.

## No paralog is itself a selective dependency

```{r own-table}
o2 <- own[, c("gene", "mean_sclc", "mean_other", "delta", "fdr", "selective")]
names(o2) <- c("Gene", "Mean SCLC", "Mean other", "Delta", "FDR", "Selective")
kable(o2, digits = 4)
```

MYC is strongly essential in both groups but **less** so in SCLC
(delta `r sprintf("%+.3f", own$delta[own$gene == "MYC"])`); MYCN and MYCL sit
near zero everywhere. Nothing in this analysis supports intervening on the
paralogs themselves.

## Two domains were excluded on evidence

The **transcriptional** domain was dropped as lineage-confounded at both
aggregate and per-gene level. The **network** domain failed both of its
pre-conditions: only `r netfeas$n_sclc_lines` SCLC lines have CCLE expression,
below what tree-ensemble inference needs, and MYC expression tracks NE state
across those lines (rho `r netfeas$myc_vs_ne_rho`) — the same structure that
barred a tumour-based network.

# Evidence integration {#sec-m8}

```{r fig-m8}
#| fig-cap: "Evidence convergence is real but too diffuse to attribute to any gene."
fig("fig04_moes_null")
```

MOES was specified as a four-domain, two-stage, weight-free Robust Rank
Aggregation. It runs on **`r dg("domains_admitted")` domains**, of which
**`r dg("paralog_resolved_domains")`** attributes evidence to a paralog.

Two things were verified before any score was believed. The cis layer was rebuilt
and asserted to reproduce the committed regulons exactly for all three paralogs.
The n = 2 RRA closed form used in the permutation loops was checked against
`RobustRankAggreg` (maximum absolute difference 1.1e-15).

## Convergence is real

```{r moes-conc}
mg <- moesglob[, c("paralog", "max_ratio", "global_p")]
names(mg) <- c("Paralog", "Max top-K overlap vs chance", "Global p")
kable(mg, digits = 3)
```

The global p compares the maximum overlap ratio over K against the permutation
distribution of that same maximum, controlling family-wise error across the
curve. Counting pointwise exceedances would badly overstate this — the K values
are nested, so one excursion produces a run of them.

## It does not localise to genes

**No gene reaches FDR < `r CFG$moes$fdr_threshold` for any paralog.** The best
FDR achieved is `r sprintf("%.3f", min(moesrank$fdr))`.

```{r moes-pc}
p2 <- moespc[, c("signal_fraction", "layer_rho", "min_fdr", "n_fdr05")]
names(p2) <- c("Injected signal", "Layer rho", "Min FDR", "Genes FDR < 0.05")
kable(p2, digits = 3)
```

A positive control blending synthetic signal into the functional layer gives a
monotone graded response, so the per-gene null is a property of the evidence, not
a dead pipeline. The signal is present in the shape the aggregate test detects
and absent in the shape the per-gene test requires: **aggregate detectable,
per-gene unattributable.**

## Two degeneracies, stated

At two domains, **two-stage RRA is degenerate** — stage 2 has nothing to
aggregate that stage 1 did not — and **leave-one-domain-out reduces to
single-domain rankings**. Neither is the check specified at M1, which assumed
four domains.

Because the functional vector is identical for all three paralogs, it pulls every
ranking toward the same genes. Paralogs agree far more closely in MOES than in
the chromatin that actually distinguishes them, so any apparent
paralog-specificity in a MOES ranking would be chromatin under a multi-omics
label.

## No hub table is reported

Presenting the head of a distribution whose best FDR is
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(moesrank$fdr))` as prioritised hubs would be the most
misleading output available here. The full ranking with its FDR column is written
to `data/metadata/moes_ranking.csv` so the absence is inspectable.

# Spatial coherence {#sec-m9}

```{r fig-m9}
#| fig-cap: "Lineage dominance reproduces in spatial data, on the one regulon the panel can measure."
fig("fig_s04_spatial")
```

Restricted orthogonal validation only. Two GeoMx DSP cohorts on a targeted
~1,800-gene panel.

```{r m9-cov}
u <- m9cov[!duplicated(m9cov$paralog), c("paralog", "measured", "regulon_size", "coverage_fraction", "scoreable")]
u$coverage_fraction <- pct(u$coverage_fraction)
names(u) <- c("Paralog", "Measured", "Regulon size", "Coverage", "Scoreable")
kable(u)
```

**Two of three regulons cannot be scored at all.** MYCL1 misses the coverage
floor by 0.4 percentage points and MYC clears it by 1.2, against a threshold this
project itself raised mid-way. These are knife-edge verdicts and are reported as
such. Every spatial number below is a 56-gene proxy for MYC, not a measurement of
the 500-gene regulon.

A limit that cannot be engineered away: slides are named for two patients and the
deposit carries no per-ROI patient label, so within-slide variance is an **upper
bound** on within-tumour variance. Only three slides in one cohort carry a single
identifier; the other cohort has none.

```{r m9-tables}
kable(m9coh[, c("cohort","subset","n_roi","n_slides","between_slide_r2","within_slide_r2")],
      digits = 3, col.names = c("Cohort","Subset","ROIs","Slides","Between-slide R2","Within-slide R2"))
kable(m9var[, c("cohort","n_roi","unique_myc","unique_lineage","full_r2")],
      digits = 4, col.names = c("Cohort","ROIs","unique R2 MYC","unique R2 lineage","Full R2"))
```

On the only interpretable subset,
`r pct(m9coh$within_slide_r2[m9coh$subset == "single-patient slides" & !is.na(m9coh$within_slide_r2)], 0)`
of the MYC regulon score varies **within a single tumour** — it is substantially a
regional property. On three slides this is an estimate, not a precise quantity.

Lineage dominance reproduces: unique R²
`r sprintf("%.3f and %.3f", m9var$unique_lineage[1], m9var$unique_lineage[2])` for
lineage against
`r sprintf("%.3f and %.3f", m9var$unique_myc[1], m9var$unique_myc[2])` for MYC, in
tissue with different chemistry, normalisation and gene panel.

# Pre-registered controls: outcome {#sec-controls}

The contract declared controls before any result existed. Reporting them
faithfully includes reporting the ones that were not met.

```{r controls-table}
ct <- data.frame(
  Control = c("Negative (M8 hard gate)", "Positive", "Benchmark: HALLMARK_MYC_TARGETS",
              "Benchmark: Jung 2017 signature", "M5 sanity gate"),
  Declared = c("Paralog-shared housekeeping promoters must not rank as paralog-specific hubs",
               "Top MYC hubs consistent with the MYC-BCL2/MCL1 apoptotic-priming axis (Dammert 2019)",
               "Paralog-blind comparator for regulon coherence",
               "18-gene paralog-blind MYC-activity comparator",
               "Re-derived region counts within a defensible range of the published values"),
  Outcome = c("**VACUOUS — no evidence either way**", "**NOT MET**", "MET",
              "**NOT DONE**", "3 PASS / 1 FAIL"))
kable(ct)
```

**The negative control cannot be scored.** It asks that housekeeping promoters
not rank as paralog-specific hubs. Since MOES produces no hubs at all, nothing
can fail it. The best-ranked housekeeping gene sits at MOES rank 171 with
FDR 0.94 — comfortably unremarkable — but a control that cannot fail provides no
evidence about specificity, and recording it as "passed" would be the same
vacuous-pass error this project caught once already in a genome-build assertion.
It is recorded as uninformative.

**The positive control is not met.** BCL2 appears in the **MYCN** regulon rather
than MYC, and its best MYC MOES rank is 128 at FDR 0.93. MCL1 is in no regulon.
The MYC→BCL2/MCL1 axis does not emerge from this analysis. Given that MOES
resolves nothing at gene level, this is consistent with the null rather than
independent evidence against the axis — but it is not a positive result and is
not presented as one.

# What is and is not established

**Established here.**

- Paralog-resolved regulons can be built from public bedGraph-only chromatin data
  and are internally coherent in the lines they come from.
- Those regulons **lose paralog identity** in patient tumours, and lineage state
  accounts for it. Replicated in two cohorts, with power.
- The confound is present at chromatin, cell-line, gene and spatial level — it is
  not an artefact of one scoring choice.
- Regulon genes **collectively** carry SCLC-selective dependency; no paralog is
  itself a selective dependency, and MYC is *less* essential in SCLC than
  elsewhere.
- The MYC regulon is neurogenesis-weighted (reproducing prior work); the MYCN
  regulon is not (a discordance with prior work).
- Roughly a third of the MYC regulon score varies within a single tumour.

**Not established, and not claimed.**

- No prioritised hub list. Evidence convergence is real in aggregate and
  unattributable at gene level.
- Nothing about MYCN or MYCL1 in spatial data — they are unmeasurable on that
  panel.
- Nothing about causation, treatment selection, or outcome.
- Criterion 3 of the M5 gate is a partial reproduction: direction yes, magnitude
  no.

**Left undone.** The drug-response association declared under Aim 3 was not
carried out, and the Jung 2017 benchmark signature was never curated from the
source publication. Both are recorded as gaps rather than quietly dropped.

# Limitations {#sec-limits}

1. **Two contributing ChIP lines each for MYCN and MYCL1** against five for MYC.
   Cis-layer coverage is correspondingly uneven and bounds what could have been
   found for the smaller paralogs.
2. **No *de novo* peak calling.** Signal is quantified over a shared
   ATAC-defined universe, which is ~84% distal by construction and compresses
   distal-fraction contrasts.
3. **The spatial panel measures ~1,800 targets.** Two of three regulons fall
   below the coverage gate; the third clears it by 1.2 percentage points.
4. **Slide is not tumour** in the spatial cohorts, so within-tumour variance is
   an upper bound.
5. **The spatial NE score rests on 3 of 10 markers**; the rest are off-panel.
6. **Bootstrap rank intervals resample cis links only.** The functional domain is
   held fixed because its per-gene values are precomputed summaries, so reported
   intervals understate total uncertainty.
7. **One line is absent from DepMap**, leaving the MYC-expressing arm of gate
   criterion 3 at n = 2 and precluding any significance test there.

# Reproducibility {#sec-repro}

```{r repro}
rp <- data.frame(
  Element = c("Environment", "Data", "Genome build", "Figures", "Decisions", "Release gate"),
  Approach = c(
    "renv.lock pins every package; `renv::restore()` from a clean clone",
    "no data in version control; download scripts plus checksum manifest",
    "hg19 asserted at every coordinate step; lifts logged with loss rates",
    paste0(nrow(figman), " figures, each regenerated by a named script and recorded in figures/figure_manifest.csv"),
    "every deviation from the frozen specification carries a numbered decision-log entry",
    "`bash scripts/07_figures/99_build_all.sh` rebuilds and verifies the full figure set"))
kable(rp)
```

The figure build driver gates on three conditions: any script exiting non-zero,
any accessibility check reporting failure, and any manifest row without both
files on disk. It was tested by making it fail — injecting an unsatisfiable
colourblind threshold — rather than by assuming it works.

Figure PNGs are byte-reproducible on re-run; PDFs differ only in an embedded
creation timestamp.

# Decisions and audit trail

Every methodological deviation is recorded in
[`docs/decision_log.md`](docs/decision_log.md), which at the time of writing holds
numbered entries D-001 through D-042. `scripts/00_setup/audit_decisions.sh`
re-checks each recorded decision against the current state of the repository.

Several entries record errors caught and corrected rather than decisions taken
cleanly — a palette that failed the project's own accessibility check, a canonical
results table left stale while two audit checks defended the staleness, and a
conclusion about evidence convergence that was too strong on first pass and
corrected. These are left legible on purpose.
